title: Did This Writer Finally Solve The Black Dahlia Mystery?

segments.text: In January 1947, the body of Elizabeth Short, later known as the Black Dahlia, was found in a vacant lot in Los Angeles.
She was twenty-two years old when she was murdered, and the case remains one of the most infamous unsolved crimes in American history.
According to the book covered in this video, the writer claims to have identified the killer through newly examined archival records.
The investigation for this theory focuses on suspects connected to Hollywood and local medical professionals in 1940s Los Angeles.
Police reports from 1947 note that the body had been surgically bisected, which led investigators to suspect someone with anatomical knowledge.
Over the decades, more than one hundred and fifty people have confessed to the murder, but none were definitively proven to be the killer.
The video argues that the writer's proposed solution rests on three key pieces of evidence that earlier investigators overlooked.
Thanks for watching, and don't forget to subscribe for more true crime deep dives.
